cpdat_context.interpretation: Source product-composition records, not current product availability, purchase prevalence, actual exposure, or concentration.

human_cumulus_cell_study.population: Primary cumulus cells collected from 26 women undergoing ICSI
human_cumulus_cell_study.reported_effect: At 20 micrograms/mL, the abstract reports decreased BUB1B, CDC20 and HAS2 expression, increased TRIB3 and LUM, and more anti-CASP3-positive cells compared with control.
human_cumulus_cell_study.source_limit: Primary abstract and publisher excerpt only; full article and complete outcome tables were not obtained. The authors describe 20 micrograms/mL as very high and supra-physiological.
human_cumulus_cell_study.molar_conversion: Approximately 87.6 micromolar using BPA molecular weight 228.29 g/mol.

bronchial_cell_study.model: Immortalized human bronchial epithelial BEAS-2B cells
bronchial_cell_study.reported_effect: BUB1B transcript and protein decreased; the study also reports dose-dependent loss of cell viability under BPA exposure.
bronchial_cell_study.source_limit: No chromosome-segregation, spindle-checkpoint, BUB1B-variant, MVA or muscle endpoint. The same paper's separate TCGA analysis found BUB1B higher in tumors than normal tissue, while BPA-treated BEAS-2B showed lower BUB1B; these distinct comparisons do not establish a BPA-caused tumor mechanism. Docking is predictive and the paper's broader exposure-to-lung-cancer claims are described as primarily correlative.

competitive_decision.disposition: Adverse-exposure comparator; not a BUB1B restoration candidate.
competitive_decision.reason: The reported direction is lower BUB1B in non-MVA cell models, without evidence of improved checkpoint function or chromosome fidelity. Cytotoxicity and exposure context prevent treating gene reduction as a selective mechanism.
competitive_decision.patient_or_ordinary_use_inference: Not established. No result transfers to the patient's alleles, MVA muscle, or ordinary consumer-product exposure.
